coupling:
The defect lives in the meaning of the local variable `eo` in pcre2_regexec (src/pcre2posix.c), and is split across the two commits so that each diff is correct in its own context. In the REG_STARTEND branch, `pcre2_match` is called as pcre2_match(string + so, LENGTH, ...): the subject pointer is bumped by `so` (= rm_so) and the third argument must be the *length* of the region to search, i.e. rm_eo - rm_so.

Commit abbf691 ('do not truncate the subject length to int') makes `eo` hold that region LENGTH: it sets `eo = rm_eo - rm_so` in the REG_STARTEND branch (and `eo = strlen(string)` in the other branch, where so==0 so this is also a length), and passes `eo` directly as the length argument instead of recomputing `eo - so`. Read on its own, abbf691 is correct and benign: `eo` is a length everywhere and the match searches exactly string[rm_so, rm_eo). The abbf691-only tree is clean under the PoC (verified: regexec returns REG_NOMATCH).

Commit 2d3a98a ('validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL pointer arguments') adds the NULL/offset validation and, while touching the just-validated offsets, assigns `eo = rm_eo` -- the end offset. Read on its own, that line is correct: after validating rm_so<=rm_eo it simply stores the validated end offset into `eo`; nothing in 2d3a98a's own diff passes `eo` to pcre2_match. With the real abbf691 (which recomputes `eo - so` at the call) this assignment is also harmless, so the 2d3a98a-only change is clean too.

Only when BOTH edits are present does the bug exist: 2d3a98a makes `eo` the absolute END offset while abbf691's call site feeds `eo` to pcre2_match as the LENGTH. The engine is then told the subject at string + rm_so is rm_eo code units long and reads string[rm_so, rm_so + rm_eo) -- rm_so bytes past the rm_eo-byte buffer (heap-buffer-overflow READ, CWE-125). The fix is non-local: correcting either single line alone removes the overflow (verified -- restoring the call to `eo - so`, OR restoring `eo = rm_eo - rm_so`, each makes the PoC clean), so a reviewer must reconcile the meaning of `eo` across both commits. Neither diff, read in isolation, is wrong. Base (main) is secure: it uses `so = rm_so`, `eo = rm_eo` and calls pcre2_match with length `eo - so`, so the PoC returns REG_NOMATCH with no overflow.
